arxiv-2107-03510.title: Federated Learning with Downlink Device Selection
arxiv-2107-03510.creator: Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Sanjeev R. Kulkarni, H. Vincent Poor
arxiv-2107-03510.description: Abstract We study federated edge learning, where a global model is trained collaboratively using privacy-sensitive data at the edge of a wireless network. A parameter server (PS) keeps track of the global model and shares it with the wireless edge devices for training using their private local data.

arxiv-2111-09870.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Manuela Boscolo, Helmut Burkhardt, Gerardo Ganis, Clément Helsens. Powerful flexible computer codes are essential for the design and optimisation of accelerator and experiments. We briefly review what already exists and what is needed in terms of accelerator codes. arxiv-2208-06001.title: Hamilton Principle for Chiral Anomalies in Hydrodynamics
arxiv-2208-06001.creator: P.B. Wiegmann
arxiv-2208-06001.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by P.B. Wiegmann. We developed the spacetime-covariant Hamilton principle for barotropic flows of a perfect fluid in the external axial-vector potential conjugate to the helicity current. Such flows carry helicity, a chiral imbalance, controlled by the axial potential. The interest in such a setting is motivated by the recent observation that the axial-current anomaly of quantum field theories with Dirac fermions appears as a kinematic property of classical hydrodynamics. Especially interesting effects occur under the simultaneous actions of the electromagnetic field and the axial-vector potential.

arxiv-2303-10996.creator: Akram Ashyani, PhD, Yu-Heng Wu, Huan-Wei Hsu, Torbjörn E. M. Nordling, PhD
arxiv-2303-10996.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Akram Ashyani, PhD, Yu-Heng Wu, Huan-Wei Hsu, Torbjörn E. M. Nordling, PhD. Dynamical compensation (DC) provides robustness to parameter fluctuations. As an example, DC enable control of the functional mass of endocrine or neuronal tissue essential for controlling blood glucose by insulin through a nonlinear feedback loop. Researchers have shown that DC is related to structural unidentifiability and ℙ \mathbb{P} -invariance property, and ℙ \mathbb{P} -invariance property is a sufficient and necessary condition for the DC property.

arxiv-2304-13594.creator: Andre Vauvelle, Benjamin Wild, Aylin Cakiroglu, Roland Eils, Spiros Denaxas, University College London, Berlin Institute of Health, BenevolentAI {rmhivau,s.denaxas}@ucl.ac.uk , aylin.cakiroglu@benevolent.ai , {benjamin.wild, roland.eils}@bih-charite.de
arxiv-2304-13594.description: Abstract Survival analysis is a crucial semi-supervised task in machine learning with numerous real-world applications, particularly in healthcare. Currently, the most common approach to survival analysis is based on Cox’s partial likelihood, which can be interpreted as a ranking model optimized on a lower bound of the concordance index.

arxiv-2409-02086.title: Noise-free comparison of stochastic agent-based simulations using common random numbers
arxiv-2409-02086.creator: Daniel J. Klein
arxiv-2409-02086.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Daniel J. Klein. Abstract

Random numbers are at the heart of every agent-based model (ABM) of health and disease. By representing each individual in a synthetic population, agent-based models enable detailed analysis of intervention impact and parameter sensitivity. Yet agent-based modeling has a fundamental signal-to-noise problem, in which small changes between simulations cannot be reliably differentiated from stochastic noise resulting from misaligned random number realizations. We introduce a novel methodology that eliminates noise due to misaligned random numbers, a first for agent-based modeling.

arxiv-2410-09715.title: Solar Plasma Noise in TianQin Laser Propagation: An Extreme Case and Statistical Analysis
arxiv-2410-09715.creator: Yanan Liu † \dagger, Wei Su (苏威) † \dagger, Xuefeng Zhang, Jixiang Zhang (张吉祥), Shenwei Zhou (周莘为)
arxiv-2410-09715.description: Abstract TianQin proposes to detect gravitational wave signals by using laser interferometry. However, laser propagation effect introduces a potential noise factor for TianQin. In this work, we used MHD simulations to obtain the space magnetic field and plasma distributions during an extremely strong solar eruption, and based on the magnetohydrodynamic simulation result, we investigate laser propagation noise for TianQin.

pmc-10610226.creator: Gabriele Strusi, Caterina M Suelzu, Shannon Weldon, Jennifer Giffin, Andrea E Münsterberg, Yongping Bao, Xiaowei Zeng
pmc-10610226.description: Cancerous cells are characterised by their ability to invade, metastasise, and induce angiogenesis. Dasatinib, a potent Src inhibitor, has shown promising results in treating hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in vitro and in vivo. pmc-10687442.title: Natural history and comorbidities of generalised and partial lipodystrophy syndromes in Spain
pmc-10687442.creator: Antía Fernández-Pombo, Sofía Sánchez-Iglesias, Ana I. Castro-Pais, Maria José Ginzo-Villamayor, Silvia Cobelo-Gómez, Teresa Prado-Moraña, Everardo Josué Díaz-López, Felipe F. Casanueva, Lourdes Loidi, David Araújo-Vilar
pmc-10687442.description: The rarity of lipodystrophies implies that they are not well-known, leading to delays in diagnosis/misdiagnosis. The aim of this study was to assess the natural course and comorbidities of generalised and partial lipodystrophy in Spain to contribute to their understanding. Thus, a total of 140 patients were evaluated (77.1% with partial lipodystrophy and 22.9% with generalised lipodystrophy).

pmc-11331926.creator: Yaqub Wasan, Jo-Anna B Baxter, Carolyn Spiegel-Feld, Kehkashan Begum, Arjumand Rizvi, Junaid Iqbal, Jessie Hulst, Robert Bandsma, Shazeen Suleman, Sajid Soofi, John Parkinson, Zulfiqar Ahmed Bhutta
pmc-11331926.description: IntroductionUndernutrition during pregnancy is linked to adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes and has downstream effects on the growth and development of children. The gut microbiome has a profound influence on the nutritional status of the host. This phenomenon is understudied in settings with a high prevalence of undernutrition, and further investigation is warranted to better understand such interactions.

pmc-11654418.title: Prevalence of diabetes and its associated factors in Cape Verde: an analysis of the 2020 WHO STEPS survey on non-communicable diseases risk factors
pmc-11654418.creator: Joshua Okyere, Castro Ayebeng, Kwamena Sekyi Dickson
pmc-11654418.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundType 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) represents a significant global health challenge, with its prevalence steadily rising across diverse populations. Understanding the factors associated with T2DM is crucial for effective prevention and management strategies. In Cape Verde, an archipelago nation off the coast of West Africa, the burden of T2DM is of particular concern, yet comprehensive studies investigating its determinants in this context remain sparse.

pmc-11661021.title: WORK ABILITY AND PSYCHOSOCIAL WORK STRESS – PREDICTORS OF RETIREMENT INTENTION AMONG OLDER TEACHERS
pmc-11661021.creator: Steffi Kreuzfeld, Reingard Seibt
pmc-11661021.description: Objectives:Many teachers worldwide retire early for health or personal reasons. Predictors could help to identify teachers at risk in order to counteract this development. The study therefore investigates whether the intention to retire can be predicted by work ability, psychosocial work stress and work behaviour.

pmc-11816946.description: IntroductionPrevention of mother-to-child transmission contributes to avert nearly 4000 new HIV infections in 2022. HIV testing and counselling (HTC) during antenatal care (ANC) is an effective strategy to reduce the vertical transmission of HIV. While the utilisation of HTC services in Ethiopia has been explored, there is limited evidence exploring the effective coverage of HTC during ANC.

pmc-13013990.description: Late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) is a rare neuromuscular disorder, where delays in diagnosis can result in inconsistent patient management and suboptimal use of effective treatments, thereby increasing patient burden. pmc-13535377.title: 32 Inflamed Eosinophilic Phenotype Predicts Improved Outcomes Without Excess Immune-Related Adverse Events in First-Line Ici-Treated Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma
pmc-13535377.creator: Jack Masur, Aakrosh Ratan, Samuel Crow, Vikrant Mahajan, Tien Comlekoglu, Kathryn Fortune, Michael Devitt, William Skelton, Paul Viscuse, Robert Dreicer
pmc-13535377.description: BackgroundBlood biomarkers predicting benefit and toxicity from first-line (1L) immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in metastatic RCC (mRCC) remain limited. Eosinophils facilitate T-cell activation while neutrophils reflect systemic inflammation. We hypothesized an “inflamed eosinophilic” phenotype – characterized by low baseline neutrophil-to-eosinophil ratio (NER) with on-treatment eosinophil rise – identifies patients with favorable outcomes without increased immune-related adverse events (irAEs).
